quest.title: Dune-Entombed Fecundity: Part I
quest.description: With the help of the Tanit, you prepare to enter Mt. Damavand in search of the secrets that lie buried within the Eternal Oasis...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, how'd you sleep?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... Why did Liloupar have to use all those strange metaphors about bugs and scorpions? Took Paimon half a night to get them out of her head!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Haha... Glad you guys got some rest. I sure didn't.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Huh? And who asked you to get up in the middle of the night to go find Matriarch Babel?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Hmph. Wrong way around. She came to find me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What did Matriarch Babel want from you?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Ah... It was an urgent... thing.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Some matters concerning the... elders of the tribe, you know?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Oh... I see we have happened upon some open secret.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Matriarch Babel spoke briefly with me last night. What we must do next is use the tunnels in the dunes to enter the underground portions of the Eternal Oasis.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Indeed... My Master, Al-Ahmar, once created a most intricate system of canals, shaped to provide irrigation for the soil of the mortal kingdoms...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Before the dune was encased in sandstorms, before Al-Ahmar was naught but dust, this place rolled with hills most fecund and verdant.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: But those canals have long run dry. Fortunately, that lends them to our purposes quite well, allowing entry to the foundations of the Oasis within the dunes.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: So Matriarch Babel has finally made her decision.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: #It's because {NICKNAME} reclaimed the Jinni. She can serve as our guide. Moreover, my tongue's as clever as that of a mockingbird's, but you should know that by now.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I indeed witnessed this occurrence, my master, but I thought there was little need to go into detail about it with you.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Alright. Let's go and discuss the rest of the details with Matriarch Babel, then.

choices.text: Not great. I kept thinking about cards every time I closed my eyes.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: And yet you were quite happy to play...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Because if you're gonna play, you should play hard! Paimon was having fun watching from the sides, too!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: #You've arrived, {NICKNAME}. I hope that our hospitality hasn't disappointed you.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Ah, Jeht. While you're here, I shall entrust the great task of apprehending the traitor Aderfi to you...

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: I suspect that the recent spike in traitors within the tribe has something to do with the interference of those who hail from the snowlands.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You mean the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Fatui... Their influence spreads even here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're just like those... toads or centipedes Liloupar keeps talking about... We keep running into them everywhere we go!

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Initially, they approached our merchants under the banner of trade. Then, before long, they started meddling in our affairs... Annoying as it is, the forces behind them are indeed powerful.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Prior to the present, we had already pushed the northerners out of our territory, forbidding them from appearing on our hunting grounds to prevent them from further harming our people.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Yet, they continue to circle us in the desert like hyenas. I don't know if they seek treasure or an alliance from us... Regardless, they are dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I got it. I'll return with additional information or a newly claimed life.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: "And."

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Information, and a newly claimed life.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Ahem... However, the Fatui are not the most important segment of today's conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, the task I bade of you today... I believe that Azariq has already gone over the broad strokes with you.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Indeed, Matriarch Babel.

dialogues.speaker: Babel
dialogues.text: Good, but I must warn you still that the path ahead is fraught with dangers... Our scouts have discovered signs that many Wenut may be active in the area.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: #Be at ease, I will guide {M#them}{F#them} down a safe path.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Wenut are extremely dangerous creatures. Approach them with caution. They may attack you upon being drawn by the Jinni's presence.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Speak not of me as if I am some manner of calamity, desert-wench!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: My master, I will be alert on your behalf. If you come under assault by these Wenut... I may yet be able to rally my strength and defend you.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #I've got your back too, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! Suddenly, we've got two handy sidekicks. Hehe.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Esteemed Liloupar... After entering the foundations of the Eternal Oasis, we must rely on your power to guide the group.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: The ruins of the canals may yet hide your... fragments.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Indeed. Of this I am aware... But I am curious as to how this knowledge came unto you.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: You learned this from "outsiders," did you not?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ha! Worry not! Robbing a few bookish researchers, parting a merchant camp with the maps they have brought with them... These are tricks of an old trade for a desert-dweller! I understand! Ahahaha!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Thank you for granting me this boon of knowledge. It shall yet lead me to old memories and power both. But I will be watching you, and that lad of yours.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Liloupar, what's wrong with you? Matriarch Babel only organized this expedition to ensure that I can lay my parents to rest! How can you just... slander her like this?

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Jeht!

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: My apologies, esteemed Liloupar. I understand your misgivings, and will endeavor to win your trust...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Do as you will. I seek respite!

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Ahem. Very well. Do not let me forestall your departure. Leave as soon as you are able.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: I'll be your guide and help to expel the Wenut, but I won't be heading into the forbidden zone. Sorry.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: I respect Azariq's considerations. The remains left by a god long past... That is something not lightly disturbed by the likes of us, who yearn only to stand vigil over this tomb. This most unpalatable task must fall to you.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Thanks for this opportunity, Matriarch Babel.

response.speaker: Babel
response.text: Yes... I hope for your safe return.

talks.objective: Descend to the innermost depths of the Eternal Oasis in Mt. Damavand
Reach the entrance of Mt. Damavand
Talk to Jeht and the others

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Next, you can just keep going into the depths of the canyon. The tunnel leading to the foundations of the Eternal Oasis should be right there.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Hmm... {NICKNAME}, beware of sandstorms. In canyons like these, the wind-flung grains sting worse than those flung by the winds on the open sands.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Be at ease. I shall protect my master. Let us progress.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Well, I'm gonna split now. You guys stay alert and stay safe.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Thanks. You too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Azariq! You're the one who should be staying safe, walking through the desert alone and all. Don't get eaten by Wenut!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: This is a Tanit camp... It even has the tribe's markings.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Matriarch Babel must've sent someone here ahead of us.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Oh, ho? What's this? Someone appears to be less attuned to the traditions they so claim to practice than they'd like...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there something wrong with the campsite?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... What's wrong with the campsite? Paimon's not seeing anything here.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: She dispatched people to comb this area before our arrival. However, I perceive that they never made it out. Perhaps it is because of such that this place was marked as "forbidden."

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Which means that this area was forbidden for matters of practicality, and not terrors wrought of superstition.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: As for why she sent people here with regularity prior... It could not just be to sate the desire of young Jeht here... More camps lie ahead, I would warrant.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: ...We'll ask Matriarch Babel about this once we get back. For now, we keep moving.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What... What is this...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Though I really don't want to act without thinking things through, I have a feeling that if we want to continue, we'll need to activate this thing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, but what if it's dangerous?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: This is a water-pumping mechanism. It was used to attune to the flow and vectors of water... Though now, water's place in its pipes has been usurped by sand.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: *sigh* As surely as you are witness, this once was a lush garden, in a time when the flowing springs had yet to become a fleeting rarity amongst the sands.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Enough talk. I think I may yet be able to spark function back into this mechanism... Allow me to try, my master.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It sure sounds like this place is familiar to Liloupar. {NICKNAME}, let's just let her give it a go!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Look there. Those tunnels. I'm thinking... of connecting them and clearing the accumulated sand. I think that might open a path for us.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ah, a reckless thought, born of ignorance. Still, the plan is worth a try.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You're getting on my nerves, Jinni.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It is my acknowledgment you are receiving, little one.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Aren't you the little one here!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jeht's young and Liloupar's small, so the way Paimon sees it, they're both little ones.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: By that logic, seeing that you're both young and small, that makes you the littlest one!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What? D—Don't bring Paimon into your squabbles! {NICKNAME}! Paimon's not little, right?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hah... How adorable...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: The path ahead lies beneath the sands.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What... Oh, it's been buried... It'll take years for just us few to dig it out.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Fret not. Let us hunt about for mechanisms nearby that might help drain the sand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure! Let's go!

talks.objective: Find another way to enter the central area

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the shard of light merges with Liloupar's magic bottle, you feel a little of your own power being pulled away...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Through the Jinni's entranced eyes, you see a ragged shepherd boy along with a dancing maiden, her presence resplendent like a limpid gem beneath the moon's gaze...\nFestering hatred assails your senses, before alchemizing into primal, burning love in a sudden instant...\nSuch love cannot be contained by the vessel of a mortal. It is an emotion that can swallow one whole.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "Then, mortal... What desire of yours can I make manifest?"

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Are you alright? Answer me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Don't scare Paimon like that! Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Worry not... my master remains unscathed.

choices.text: Sorry, I was out of it for a moment...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{M#"Out of it?" I thought you lost consciousness!}{F#Really? I thought you were seized by something foul within the bottle!}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You worried Paimon sick!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Apologies. I did not mean to let you behold a moment so shameful. But as you might understand, I have reclaimed a portion of my memories. Now, I may guard you better.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. The light inside the bottle really does look more sprightly now.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yeah... It looks just like the lights I saw when Matriarch Babel was emerging from Azariq's tent.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...Let's change subjects.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Across the sands, there is still much of me that lies scattered. If you find it within yourself to offer me this generosity, my master, I will be beyond grateful should you collect my fragments and return me to wholeness.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: In areas around a Jinni's fragments, a spot of green should flourish...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: This is because we Jinn always release energy around us to create an environment conducive to our slumber. I hope you shall bear this in mind.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I will.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: You have my thanks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon will help too! Paimon's eyesight is second to none! Don't worry about it.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ah... I am invigorated! Come. Let us delve deeper.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yeah. Let's go.

choices.text: It was a memory. Someone else's memory...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Huh? I don't... What are you saying?

talks.objective: Head to the depths of the mountain
Talk to Jeht and the others

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... What a cavern. Was this place full of water too?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: A mechanism once built to sustain a dream of eternity, to supply the oasis, forever and always. It was once propelled by water but is now driven only by sand.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: King Deshret left his glass goblet here, at the center of this place. The tales speak of him bidding farewell to joy, and leaving his cup behind here as a receptacle to contain past traumas and memories...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: And those traumas and memories protected the eternal sleep of my mistress, the Lord of Flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Was that... something that happened in your time?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hm? I suppose, but the details elude my recollection, what with my memories being as scattered as they are...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Then, we need to go down there and activate that... glass?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Patience. See how there are still two points of entry? Perhaps there are more mechanisms that we need to disable.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Prithee have faith in my intuition, dear master.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... So, how are we going to get through now?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmm... Looks like all we can do is head back to the surface and find another path. Uh... Jinni, can you find another way leading to the other two tunnel entrances?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I dare not claim to be certain. With loose confidence... I believe so.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Alright. Good. Then, we'd best get back to the surface and start plotting a new path. Any objections?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: What do you think, my master?

choices.text: (Return to the surface) Let's go back first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright...

choices.text: I need to look around some more.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Your words, my will, my master.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{M#What? Did you find anything new? Heh, care to share?}{F#You know, I actually look forward to exploring together like this, and that's something I haven't felt in while, let me tell you... And there's something new there too.}

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: We're going, then. Keep up.

choices.text: I need to stay and explore.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Alright. Be careful. I'll wait for you here.

talks.objective: Talk to Azariq and the others

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Huh... The air outside is crisp!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: What difference is there? 'Tis still as dry and hot as before...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You aren't a desert-dweller. Of course you don't get it!
Hey, little wildcat!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Over here! If this isn't a coincidence!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Azariq! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Exploring and scouting, same as always. What, is running into another explorer in the desert strange to you?

choices.text: It is a little suspect, actually.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Running into sand and scorpions is normal. Running into the same person all the time is one coincidence too many for Paimon...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Haha, alright! Come over and have some food, drink some water. You all must be tired.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmm. You got any plans after this? You wanna come with us?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Come with you? You've found a path?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...Don't tell...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Of course!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Heh, never mind that for now. The sky's dimming. We should rest. The path will still be there tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Ha. You're right about that!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Speaking of which... Liloupar, I'm curious but never got to ask...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Why do you hate Matriarch Babel so much?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah. Other than {NICKNAME}, you've been mean to everyone... Especially Matriarch Babel. Every word you say is always so harsh...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: What of it? Does it displease you that I taunt your "tribe-mother" so?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Of course it does! But I want to know why...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hmm... Why, you ask?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Ha... Let me tell you a story, child.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The cold of the desert nights bears a heft to its chill, and murmurs of secrets whisper over the midnight dunes basked beneath the silvery fang of a crescent moon...\nWith a low voice, the Jinni breathes life into a tale from an age long past...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Once, a Jinni and a mortal king found themselves entwined in love, and from their union came children...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: But as time flowed, the mortal could not break the chains of power and ambition that clung to him, betraying the love of the Jinni...\nHence, on the path of revenge, she twisted the fates of her children, wreathing them in a plot to unmake their father and kingdom...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And time sailed ever onward...\nThe children of the Jinni grew to become king and queen, yet fell to the same schemes, to the same curse... Until their kingdom was finally shattered upon reaching calamity's end.\nSuch an ending, then, was that which the Jinni had orchestrated from the very beginning...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So... That was a scary story... horrifying, even. But what does this have to do with my question?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: The Jinni in the story is not so unlike Babel, is she?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Where they differ, however, is the shame and quests for renown that so compel your kind... Babel wears them like a mask, though she too is a creature of deceit. I taste it wafting from her very being.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: To her, be it son or daughter, all children are but instruments for her schemes.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: If you were absent, my master... I fear I might even be quite fond of her. But today, things are different... She threatens your safety, and so affability is beyond my sphere of virtues.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: No, Matriarch Babel isn't that kind of person...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: You have spent more time with her, and must've taken orders from her. Orders that... "the left hand" must never learn of.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Perhaps those sordid affairs were just too inconvenient for you to face or consider... But I know your follies, and stupidity does not rank amongst them. Consider these matters yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: It's fine, Jeht! Don't take this stuff so seriously. It's not like she's that much nicer to me or anything!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: And should I? To you, who are little more than a slave?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: My words have run dry... Apologies, then, if I have upset you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Umm... Maybe we just haven't been together that long? Liloupar was pretty mean to Jeht before, but she seems much nicer now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, uh... Maybe... If everyone knew more about each other, we could have a few less misunderstandings... and stuff like that?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Yeah... Let's talk about something else instead.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: S—Sure...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: What's the matter, Jeht? You're looking real distracted right now.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Nothing... Just continue...

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, what have you all discovered? Tell me — I'm curious.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well... I don't really know how to describe it to you. There are countless ancient pipes leading into the temple inside the mountain and... the legendary goblet of Al-Ahmar is there too.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: ...So, that thing was more than just a legend, huh? It really exists...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? Is that goblet valuable or something?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hah. That's not the actual goblet. It's just a mechanism holding the Eternal Oasis in stasis.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aghhh... So, it's worth nothing at all? Now Paimon's depressed.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yeah... So, that's what we've seen so far.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Then, the Eternal Oasis... was never far from us at all.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yeah... Dad always told me that he would one day enter the Eternal Oasis and find Mom again... Never thought I'd be helping him make his dream come true.

choices.text: Jebrael would be proud of you.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Him? Ha! I don't care about him! Dad was a real simpleton... This trip was for me to send him to the place where he belongs. It doesn't matter what he feels about this!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Ah... I don't know. Truth be told, I just don't know...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: My parents... Will they truly reunite in such a place? The place we're heading to... Is it just a meaningless destination that I want to reach for the sake of... because I want to console myself?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way! Jebrael would be super happy! You're helping him fulfill his wish after all...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #Whatever the case, I have you to thank, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. Thanks for... coming all this way to accompany me on this adventure. And, y'know, putting up with my... willfulness.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #{M#Ever since I lost Dad... I only feel this free when I'm with you.}{F#After Dad... left, the fear of losing my home only leaves me when I'm with you.}

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, being able to adventure with you again has been great for us, too!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: *cough* And what about me, eh? Cold and alone... Abandoned by the fire...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hahaha! Stop it! You're my family too! You really showed me how things were done when I first came to the tribe.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Hmph! This little wildcat was terrifying when she first arrived, let me tell you. Her face was like a doll. She wouldn't cry, wouldn't talk... But after spending some time messing about with me, she slowly opened up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa. So Jeht has moments of silence too? Paimon never thought that was possible!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #Stop your heckling, Paimon. Don't listen to him. You too, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Hahaha! Indeed. She didn't complain when she fell... and she didn't cry when she was hurt. Her calmness was... frankly terrifying, but her rage... When it comes... "Crash!" She's like thunder.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: What are you saying? Do you want a beating?

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: Anyway, though Jeht is young, she is far more mature than most her age. It's frankly a relief.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Alright, alright. You're full of it... *sigh* I practically died of embarrassment when I first joined the Tanit...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: The time after Dad was gone... was like a haze. Anyway, I thought I would never be able to feel normally again.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: It was all thanks to Azariq guiding me, teaching me how things worked in the tribe like a big brother that I could recover. It's been slow going...

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: That's how it was. No need to be modest!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Yeah. Dad also said he was going to tell me more stories about Mom. But now, I'm never going to get a chance to learn who she was.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: He said she was a beauty, that she was a character with countless virtues, like... "O stars high above the wasteland..."

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: "O stars high above the wasteland, O nightingales weary from the day. It's time to take off the crown of roses; Cleanse yourself with wine made from grapes."

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That's the only memory I have left of her. Dad always used to sing me this old nursery rhyme.

response.speaker: Azariq
response.text: That was lovely.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Stop it, you know I'm always out of tune!

choices.text: You sing it better than Jebrael did.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hah. I knew you'd remember. I spent a long time practicing this one. Couldn't get it down when Dad was still with us.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: After Dad... left, I, uh... Heh. Finding my pitch just got that much harder. But I still learned pretty good, didn't I?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that sounded good! Jeht's voice might be a little raspy, but it fits a soft melody like this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Hmm. Just like Jebrael.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: ...Yeah.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Alright, you should get some rest. We have lots to do tomorrow. I'll stand watch tonight.

response.speaker: Black Screen

choices.text: This is the song Jebrael liked to sing...
I imagine you're looking forward to this too, Jeht.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Of course, and that's because I'm with you guys!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Dad once said that the sands are like our home. I didn't get it at the time, but now I think I'm beginning to understand...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Home isn't perfect. Sometimes, it's downright frustrating, domineering, or even cruel. But you know you belong there.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You'll treasure its atmosphere and fear that it might leave you. You'll do anything to stop anyone from trying to tear it apart and seek care and companionship from its existence.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: It took leaving Dad's protection to learn that this is what "home" is.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I know that Dad would never abandon me and that he never lied. But people have to grow up and find new homes for themselves.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: To me, the Tanit might just be that home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Finding a new place to belong to is great, and Paimon's sure Jebrael would be happy for you! Yep!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Hey, the sun's up. Got something to show you. Follow me!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What's the hurry? And what's with the secrecy? Can't you just show us here?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, how'd you sleep?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not bad. Thanks for asking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... Why did Liloupar have to use all those strange metaphors about bugs and scorpions? Took Paimon half a night to get them out of her head!

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Haha... Glad you guys got some rest. I sure didn't.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Huh? And who asked you to get up in the middle of the night to go find Matriarch Babel?

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Hmph. Wrong way around. She came to find me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What did Matriarch Babel want from you?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Ah... It was an urgent... thing.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Some matters concerning the... elders of the tribe, you know?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Oh... I see we have happened upon some open secret.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Matriarch Babel spoke briefly with me last night. What we must do next is use the tunnels in the dunes to enter the underground portions of the Eternal Oasis.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Indeed... My Master, Al-Ahmar, once created a most intricate system of canals, shaped to provide irrigation for the soil of the mortal kingdoms...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Before the dune was encased in sandstorms, before Al-Ahmar was naught but dust, this place rolled with hills most fecund and verdant.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: But those canals have long run dry. Fortunately, that lends them to our purposes quite well, allowing entry to the foundations of the Oasis within the dunes.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: So Matriarch Babel has finally made her decision.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: #It's because {NICKNAME} reclaimed the Jinni. She can serve as our guide. Moreover, my tongue's as clever as that of a mockingbird's, but you should know that by now.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I indeed witnessed this occurrence, my master, but I thought there was little need to go into detail about it with you.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Alright. Let's go and discuss the rest of the details with Matriarch Babel, then.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Hey... It's just ahead, right? Look out, {NICKNAME}, and don't let the sand get in your mouth.

dialogues.speaker: Azariq
dialogues.text: Haha. I think you're the one who needs to worry about that! Keeping your mouth shut works better than anything in stopping that from happening!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Mind your own business!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #What? There are still more camps ahead? Hold on for a second, {NICKNAME}. I'm going to check.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: There are so many scattered ruins here... I wonder what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: If my memories had never come so undone, perhaps I could offer you enlightenment.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: But all that unfolded here, all that has not been regarded as a "lesson" by the sages of other nations... It hurts my very being.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Can Jinn feel pain too?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: The Jinn have little need for a vessel, and even less need for senses. But should we begin to connect with others... Then we will take from them their pain... Even should we not comprehend the source of it.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I know my words are beyond your understanding. There is no need for you to placate me.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I did understand you! Just... Not completely...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: There's a mechanism there. Let's go check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: My lord, I already see it! It's a fragment of mine, of my divinity and wisdom. Please... Please bring me closer!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The night flies by amidst the card games and chats.\nAs the next morning comes, you are buried in each others' pillows, asleep by the extinguished flame.
